Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the performance requirements and what Redwood will provide for qualification:  

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Latency targets: interactive chat use case — target p95 <= 300ms for first-token (streaming enabled), completion latency p95 <= 1s for responses <= 256 tokens under normal traffic.  
- Concurrency: steady-state concurrency ~60 rps, peak bursts up to 180 concurrent requests for short windows (2–5 minutes).
- Throughput: sustained throughput target ~20k tokens/minute average (model variant: Llama2-Chat-13B-quant).
- Streaming: server-driven token streaming required for the front-end (SSE/HTTP chunked). Need first-token fast paths.

Open qualification questions we promised to follow up on:
1) How Redwood measures latency: is it first-byte vs completion; do you need network e2e vs ingress measurement?
2) Failure/remedy expectations: acceptable outage definitions, service credit formula, and exclusions (maintenance, customer misconfig).
3) Reporting cadence: weekly perf summaries during pilot, monthly SLA reports post-go-live.
4) Required artifacts from SimplyMed: 48–72 hour sample traffic file (headers + timing) and example UI flows for streaming.

Attachments: traffic-sample.csv (template), draft-sla-04-01.docx (placeholder language).

Proposed next steps:

- Schedule a technical workshop (30–45m) to walk through traffic sample and streaming integration — would Tuesday 4/6 or Wednesday 4/7 work?
- Procurement contact loop-in after SLA draft is stable.

If this looks right I’ll ask Ben to add the SLA snippet and Karthik to include the telemetry points we’ll collect.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Hi Alex — quick technical clarifications from the infra side, so expectations are explicit:  

Measurement definitions (how Redwood records latency):
- Ingress timestamp: time request is received by Redwood edge (t_ingress).
- First-token timestamp: time first token is emitted by the model runtime (t_first). We record first-token latency = t_first - t_ingress.
- Completion timestamp: time final token is emitted (t_last). Completion latency = t_last - t_ingress.
- Client e2e (browser) latency is not something we measure by default; we can accept client timestamps in the sample traffic but will normalize to ingress-based timestamps for SLA calculations.

Percentiles and windows:
- We report p50/p90/p95/p99 over rolling 5-minute windows and aggregate to daily and monthly SLOs for SLA calculations.

Concurrency and throughput:
- Concurrency measured as active request count at the ingress during a 1-second sampling interval.
- Throughput measured as tokens/sec averaged over a 1-minute window, with burst detection flagged when 1-minute throughput exceeds 3x the 15-minute moving average.

Streaming specifics:
- For streaming endpoints, we expose both first-token latency and per-token inter-arrival distributions. Our streaming SLOs are based on first-token latency and 90th-percentile inter-token gap for the first 20 tokens for interactive flows.

Exclusions we typically apply for SLA calculations:
- Planned maintenance windows (documented in advance, typically 4–6 hours/mo for major upgrades).
- Force majeure and third-party outages (cloud provider).
- Customer-side misconfiguration (e.g., routing to private VPC endpoints incorrectly) — we require triage evidence.

What we need from SimplyMed to finalize the measurement spec:
1) The sample traffic CSV (client timestamps OK) — please include a sample UI flow where streaming is active.
2) Expected peak window characteristics (are bursts usually 2–5 minutes or longer?).
3) Which model variants you want measured under SLA (production vs experimental).

I’ll drop a short doc with the telemetry keys (t_ingress, t_first, t_last, request_id, model_id) into the HubSpot link; that should make the workshop concrete.

— Karthik

Alex / team — attaching a starter SLA snippet in draft-sla-04-01.docx but pasting the core language here for quick review:  

Draft — Measurement & Remedies excerpt:
- Measurement: Latency SLOs are measured at Redwood ingress (t_ingress -> t_first for first-token; t_ingress -> t_last for completion). Percentile calculations use rolling 5-minute windows and are aggregated monthly for SLA determination.
- Exclusions: Planned maintenance, force majeure, customer misconfiguration, third-party provider outages.
- Remedies: If monthly SLO availability falls below the committed threshold, Redwood will issue service credits as follows:  
  * < 99.9% monthly availability: 10% of monthly service fees
  * 99.5% - 99.9%: 20% of monthly service fees
  * < 99.5%: 50% of monthly service fees
  (Note: availability here is defined on the set of requests that meet the model and API contract and excludes the items in Exclusions.)

- Calculation: Credits are calculated against committed monthly spend on the Redwood Dedicated/Hosted plan specified in the commercial schedule. Bursty spikes that occur outside normal business hours will be analyzed; credits are only applied if the root cause is within Redwood scope.

Action items from Redwood:
- Ben to iterate SLA wording with legal (I’ll send redlines next week).
- Karthik to produce a short telemetry spec and sample queries for validation.
- Hannah to schedule the technical workshop for 4/7.

Happy to walk through the snippet on the workshop; we can make exclusions and credit thresholds mutual.

Best,
